Boston Symphony Orchestra Musicians Finalize Three-Year Labor Agreement

The agreement will remain in place until August 2029

By The Violin Channel
August 26, 2026
2 MIN READ
(PC: Robert Torres)
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:12
Instaread

The Boston Symphony Orchestra and its musicians have announced the finalization of a three-year labor agreement that will remain in effect until August 2029.

The finalization, which was announced on Tuesday, August 25th, comes after the musicians' union voted to authorize a strike, which would have been one of the few in the orchestra's 145-year history.

In a statement released by the Boston Musicians' Association, the new deal ensures an equitable relationship between the organization's management and the musicians of the orchestra, and gives the musicians a more active role in the ensemble's artistic direction and decision-making process.

The latter point comes amidst ongoing scrutiny of the BSO management, which decided not to renew Music Director Andris Nelsons’ contract in March 2026. This July, the Red Flower campaign was launched, encouraging BSO patrons to wear a rose to Tanglewood performances in solidarity with Nelsons. He will be concluding his tenure next summer at Tanglewood after 13 seasons.

"This agreement marks an important step toward a more collaborative future for the BSO," reads a joint statement from the Boston Symphony Orchestra, the Boston Musicians’ Association and the Musicians of the Boston Symphony Orchestra.

"It creates a precedent-setting partnership between musicians and management in artistic planning and centers excellence across all the work we do on our stages and in our communities. It also establishes a truly collaborative process in the search for our next music director.

"We are one institution of musicians, staff, and boards, committed to working together in partnership to advance our artistic mission, inspire audiences, and serve Boston, the Berkshires, and beyond," the statement continues. "We want to thank our audiences, donors, and partners for your continued support of the BSO."

According to bassist Todd Seeber, the chair of the BSO Players Committee, the new agreement is "an innovative and transformative path forward for American orchestras, involving players as never before in the process of artistic decision-making and planning.

“With both musicians and management working in earnest, we look forward to presenting the finest in classical music for our devoted audiences,” says Seeber.
